properties.name: Eastwatch-by-the-Sea
properties.description: The easternmost castle of the Night's Watch, where the Wall meets the sea. Jon Snow's expedition to capture a wight set out from Eastwatch, and in the season 7 finale the Night King destroyed its section of the Wall with the undead Viserion, letting the army of the dead into Westeros.

properties.name: Whitetree
properties.description: An abandoned Free Folk village built around an enormous weirwood tree, north of the Wall. It is book background that never appears in the TV series, whose Great Ranging stops instead at Craster's Keep.

properties.name: Craster's Keep
properties.description: The fortified homestead of the wildling Craster, who wed his daughters and gave his infant sons to the White Walkers. The Night's Watch sheltered there on the Great Ranging; mutineers later murdered Craster and Lord Commander Mormont, and Jon Snow wiped the mutineers out in season 4.

properties.name: Fist of the First Men
properties.description: An ancient ringfort atop a hill beyond the Wall, where the Night's Watch camped during the Great Ranging. Sam unearthed a cache of dragonglass there, and the army of the dead overran the camp at the end of season 2, leaving only a handful of survivors.

properties.name: Hardhome
properties.description: The largest Free Folk settlement, a fishing village on the Bay of Seals. Jon Snow and Tormund sailed there in season 5 to evacuate the wildlings, but the Night King's army massacred the town and he raised the fallen as wights while Jon escaped by sea.

properties.name: King's Landing
properties.description: Capital of the Seven Kingdoms and seat of the Iron Throne, sprawling above Blackwater Bay. Home to the Red Keep, the Great Sept of Baelor and Flea Bottom — and the stage for the game of thrones itself.

properties.name: Hayford Castle
properties.description: Castle seat of House Hayford, a short ride northwest of King's Landing. One of the crownland houses sworn directly to the Iron Throne, it is book background and never appears in the show.

properties.name: Rosby
properties.description: Castle and village of House Rosby on the coastal road between King's Landing and Duskendale. It is book background rather than a show location, though travelers leaving the capital northward would pass through it.

properties.name: Old Stone Bridge Inn
properties.description: A wayside inn on the road between Rosby and Duskendale, named for the ancient stone bridge beside it. Known from Brienne's search for Sansa in the books; it never appears in the show.

properties.name: Duskendale
properties.description: Port town on Blackwater Bay north of King's Landing, held by House Rykker. Famous in Targaryen history as the site of the Defiance of Duskendale against the Mad King, but the town itself is never visited in the show.

properties.name: Stokeworth
properties.description: Castle seat of House Stokeworth just north of King's Landing. In Season 5, Bronn strolls its grounds with his betrothed Lollys Stokeworth, dreaming of a lordship — until Jaime Lannister arrives to recruit him for a mission to Dorne.

properties.name: Rook's Rest
properties.description: Castle of House Staunton on the shore of Blackwater Bay, between Duskendale and Crackclaw Point. It never appears in the show and remains book background.

properties.name: The Whispers
properties.description: Ruined castle of the extinct House Crabb on Crackclaw Point, where the severed heads collected by legendary Ser Clarence Crabb were said to whisper to one another. Book background only; it is never seen in the show.

properties.name: Dragonstone
properties.description: Ancient island fortress of the Targaryens, carved with dragon shapes above a volcanic shore. Seat of Stannis Baratheon early in the war, later Daenerys' first foothold in Westeros — and it sits atop a mountain of dragonglass.

properties.name: Sharp Point
properties.description: Castle of House Bar Emmon at the tip of Massey's Hook, watching the mouth of Blackwater Bay across from Dragonstone. Book background; it does not appear in the show.

properties.name: Stonedance
properties.description: Seat of House Massey on Massey's Hook, the peninsula guarding the southern approach to Blackwater Bay. Book background; the castle is never shown or discussed in the series.

properties.name: Sunspear
properties.description: Seat of House Martell at the desert's edge by the sea. Doran Martell ruled from here until Ellaria Sand murdered him in his own gardens and seized Dorne for her vengeance.

properties.name: Water Gardens
properties.description: The Martells' pleasure palace of pools and blood-orange trees on the coast near Sunspear. Myrcella lived here as Trystane's betrothed; Jaime and Bronn's rescue turned into a brawl with the Sand Snakes in its courtyards.

properties.name: Tower of Joy
properties.description: Lonely round tower in the Red Mountains where Bran's visions showed young Ned Stark defeat Ser Arthur Dayne — and find Lyanna in a bed of blood. Jon Snow was born here, and the realm's greatest secret with him.

properties.name: Starfall
properties.description: Seat of House Dayne on the Summer Sea, home of the fallen Sword of the Morning, Ser Arthur Dayne. Its name shadows every telling of the Tower of Joy.

properties.name: Yronwood
properties.description: Seat of the proudest Dornish house after the Martells, guarding the Boneway pass. Book background only.

properties.name: Wyl
properties.description: Castle of House Wyl on the Boneway into the Dornish Marches. Book background only.

properties.name: Ghaston Grey
properties.description: Crumbling island prison of Dorne, where the Martells send men they do not wish to kill. Book background only.

properties.name: Vulture's Roost
properties.description: Ruined mountain keep once held by outlaw kings of the Red Mountains. Book background only.

properties.name: Uplands
properties.description: Seat of House Uller — Ellaria Sand's family — in the western desert. Book background only.

properties.name: Blackmont
properties.description: Castle of House Blackmont on the Torentine in the Red Mountains. Book background only.

properties.name: High Hermitage
properties.description: Mountain seat of the cadet branch of House Dayne. Book background only.

properties.name: Sandstone
properties.description: Desert castle of House Qorgyle, deep in the sands of western Dorne. Book background only.

properties.name: Skyreach
properties.description: Eyrie-like seat of House Fowler above the Prince's Pass. Book background only.

properties.name: Kingsgrave
properties.description: Castle of House Manwoody in the Red Mountains, named for a king slain at its gates. Book background only.

properties.name: Hellholt
properties.description: Grim desert stronghold where a dragon once died — Meraxes, felled by a scorpion bolt through the eye. Book background with a legacy the show's scorpions echo.

properties.name: Vaith
properties.description: Castle on the river Vaith amid the deep sands. Book background only.

properties.name: Salt Shore
properties.description: Seat of House Gargalen on the Summer Sea coast. Book background only.

properties.name: Godsgrace
properties.description: Castle of House Allyrion at the joining of the Greenblood's branches. Book background only.

properties.name: The Tor
properties.description: Seat of House Jordayne on the eastern Dornish coast. Book background only.

properties.name: Ghost Hill
properties.description: White chalk-hill castle of House Toland overlooking the Sea of Dorne. Book background only.

properties.name: Lemonwood
properties.description: Lemon-orchard seat of House Dalt near the mouth of the Greenblood. Book background only.

properties.name: Planky Town
properties.description: Floating trade town of rafts and poleboats at the Greenblood's mouth, where the orphans of the river trade. Book background only.

properties.name: Shandystone
properties.description: Abandoned holdfast in the dry hills east of the Greenblood. Book background only.

properties.name: Tall Trees Town
properties.description: Settlement of the Green Blood orphans upriver. Book background only.

properties.name: Meereen
properties.description: Greatest of the slave cities, taken by Daenerys in Season 4 and ruled from its Great Pyramid through insurgency, dragon-fire and siege. After the masters' final defeat, Slaver's Bay was renamed the Bay of Dragons.

properties.name: Astapor
properties.description: The Red City of the Good Masters, where the Unsullied were made. Daenerys bought her army here — and paid with a single word: dracarys.

properties.name: Yunkai
properties.description: The Yellow City of the Wise Masters, freed when Daario, Jorah and Grey Worm took its back gate by night. Its freedmen hailed Daenerys as Mhysa — mother.

properties.name: Vaes Dothrak
properties.description: The only city of the Dothraki, beneath the Mother of Mountains — a place where blades may not be drawn. Daenerys ate the stallion's heart here, and years later burned the khals in the temple of the Dosh Khaleen.

properties.name: Qarth
properties.description: Opulent trading city at the edge of the known world, called the greatest city that ever was or will be. Daenerys sought ships here and lost her dragons to the warlocks of the House of the Undying.

properties.name: Volantis
properties.description: Oldest and proudest of the Free Cities at the mouths of the Rhoyne. Tyrion crossed its Long Bridge and heard the red priestess Kinvara's kind preach the dragon queen; Jorah kidnapped him from one of its brothels.

properties.name: Valyria
properties.description: Shattered heart of the Valyrian Freehold, destroyed in a single day by the Doom four centuries past. Jorah and Tyrion rowed through its drowned ruins among the stone men — where Jorah was touched by grayscale.

properties.name: Naath
properties.description: Peaceful island of the butterfly people off Sothoryos — Missandei's homeland, taken from her by slavers as a child. Grey Worm sailed for it after her death, to protect her people as she could not be protected.

properties.name: Lhazarene Village
properties.description: Village of the peaceful lamb men, sacked by Drogo's khalasar in Season 1. Daenerys claimed its godswife Mirri Maz Duur — a mercy repaid with blood magic.

properties.name: Qohor
properties.description: Free City in the great forest, famed for smiths who can rework Valyrian steel. The reforging of Ice into Oathkeeper and Widow's Wail is their craft's echo in the show.

properties.name: New Ghis
properties.description: Island city of the resurgent Ghiscari, kin to the masters of Slaver's Bay. Book background only.

properties.name: Old Ghis
properties.description: Ruin of the ancient Ghiscari Empire, brought down by Valyrian dragons five thousand years before the show. The harpy of Ghis still crowns the slaver cities.

properties.name: Mantarys
properties.description: City on the demon road skirting the Valyrian ruin, whose people are said to be born twisted. Book background only.

properties.name: Elyria
properties.description: Island city on the Gulf of Grief, survivor of the Doom. Book background only.

properties.name: Tolos
properties.description: City of slingers on the Gulf of Grief. Book background only.

properties.name: Ar Noy
properties.description: Rhoynar ruin on the upper Qhoyne, long claimed by Qohor. Book background only.

properties.name: Sar Mell
properties.description: Rhoynar ruin on the river across from Volon Therys. Book background only.

properties.name: Oros
properties.description: Dead city of the Valyrian peninsula, lost in the Doom. Book background only.

properties.name: Ghozai
properties.description: Ghiscari ruin on the Isle of Cedars, drowned by the Doom's tidal waves. Book background only.

properties.name: Velos
properties.description: Ruined port on the Isle of Cedars, swallowed by the waves of the Doom. Book background only.

properties.name: Zamettar
properties.description: Abandoned Ghiscari colony on Sothoryos's northern coast. Book background only.

properties.name: Yeen
properties.description: Cyclopean ruin of oily black stone deep in Sothoryos, older than memory and shunned by all. Book background only.

properties.name: Gogossos
properties.description: Infamous ruin of the Basilisk Isles, once a Valyrian penal colony and slaver den. Book background only.

properties.name: Bhorash
properties.description: Dead Valyrian city on the demon road between Mantarys and Tolos. Book background only.

properties.name: Tyria
properties.description: Lost city of the Valyrian heartland, destroyed in the Doom. Book background only.

properties.name: Lys
properties.description: Island Free City famed for its pleasure houses, poisons and pale beauty. The strangler that killed Joffrey traces through Lysene trade; Doreah and Varys' origins touch it. Never visited on screen.

properties.name: Tyrosh
properties.description: Free City of dyers and sellswords across the sea from the Stepstones. Daario Naharis was a Tyroshi slave before the Second Sons. Mentioned often; never shown.

properties.name: Myr
properties.description: Free City renowned for lenses, lace and crossbows. Thoros of Myr carried its name across Westeros, and Varys was cut by a sorcerer in Myr as a boy.

properties.name: Pentos
properties.description: Wealthy Free City on the Narrow Sea where Daenerys was wed to Khal Drogo in the manse of Illyrio Mopatis. Later Varys and Tyrion's first stop on the road to Meereen.

properties.name: Ghoyan Drohe
properties.description: Ruined river town of the old Rhoynar civilization on the Little Rhoyne, northeast of Pentos. Book background from Tyrion's road east; not in the show.

properties.name: Norvos
properties.description: Hill-bound Free City of the bearded priests, ruled by its three great bells. Areo Hotah's homeland in the books; passing mentions in the show.

properties.name: Braavos
properties.description: Greatest and most secretive of the Free Cities, hidden in a lagoon behind the towering Titan. Home of the Iron Bank and the House of Black and White, where Arya trained with the Faceless Men.

properties.name: Lorath
properties.description: Smallest and poorest of the Free Cities, on islands in the Shivering Sea. Jaqen H'ghar claimed to be 'a man from Lorath.' Never shown.

properties.name: Ny Sar
properties.description: Drowned ruin of a Rhoynar city at the joining of the Rhoyne and the Noyne. Book background; part of the dead river civilization the show never visits.

properties.name: The Sorrows (Chroyane)
properties.description: The festival city of old Rhoyne, now a fog-bound ruin of greyscale-stricken stone men. The show relocates its stone men to the ruins of Valyria, where Jorah was infected.

properties.name: Selhorys
properties.description: River town on the Rhoyne subject to Volantis. Part of Tyrion's book journey east; the show's road to Meereen skips it.

properties.name: Valysar
properties.description: Volantene river town on the lower Rhoyne. Book background only; never seen in the series.

properties.name: Volon Therys
properties.description: River town above the mouths of the Rhoyne where, in the books, the Golden Company mustered. The show's Golden Company sails for Westeros from farther east.

properties.name: Pyke
properties.description: Seat of House Greyjoy — towers on sea-battered stacks joined by swaying rope bridges. Theon came home to it, Balon was thrown from its bridge by Euron, and the kingsmoot on its shores gave Euron the Salt Throne.

properties.name: Pebbleton
properties.description: Fishing town on Great Wyk, largest of the Iron Islands. Book background; it is never visited in the show.

properties.name: Hammerhorn
properties.description: Grim inland keep of House Goodbrother on Great Wyk, hewn from the hills above the iron mines. Book background only.

properties.name: Nagga's Ribs
properties.description: The bones of the sea dragon Nagga on the holy headland of Old Wyk, where the ironborn of legend crowned their kings. The show's kingsmoot draws on this tradition, though the site itself is never shown.

properties.name: Castle Goodbrother
properties.description: A lesser Goodbrother holdfast in the Iron Islands. Book background; never seen or named on screen.

properties.name: Ten Towers
properties.description: Seat of House Harlaw on Harlaw, the most populous of the isles — ten mismatched towers raised over generations. Home of Rodrik the Reader in the books; unseen in the show.

properties.name: Winterfell
properties.description: Ancient seat of House Stark and capital of the North, built over hot springs against the winter cold. Burned by Theon's ironborn, seized by the Boltons, retaken by Jon and Sansa — and the field of the Long Night, where the Night King shattered at Arya's hand.

properties.name: Castle Black
properties.description: Principal stronghold of the Night's Watch at the foot of the Wall. Jon Snow rose from steward to Lord Commander here — was murdered and resurrected within its walls — and rode out its gate into the true North in the series' final shot.

properties.name: White Harbor
properties.description: The North's only city and its main port, ruled by House Manderly, bannermen of the Starks. Jon and Daenerys' armies landed here on the march to Winterfell.

properties.name: Moat Cailin
properties.description: Ruined fortress guarding the causeway through the Neck — the choke point between North and South. Held by ironborn until Ramsay Bolton took it back through Theon's surrender.

properties.name: The Dreadfort
properties.description: Grim seat of House Bolton, whose banners carry the flayed man for good reason. Theon Greyjoy was unmade into Reek in its dungeons.

properties.name: Bear Island
properties.description: Forested island in the Bay of Ice, seat of House Mormont. Ten-year-old Lady Lyanna Mormont pledged its sixty-two fighting men to Jon Snow — and died killing a giant at Winterfell.

properties.name: Last Hearth
properties.description: Seat of House Umber, last castle before the Gift and the Wall. The dead reached it first in Season 8 — little Ned Umber was left pinned in the Night King's spiral.

properties.name: Karhold
properties.description: Seat of House Karstark, Stark kin who broke with Robb over Lord Rickard's execution and fought for the Boltons — until Alys Karstark knelt to Jon.

properties.name: Deepwood Motte
properties.description: Wooden motte-and-bailey of House Glover in the wolfswood, seized by Yara's ironborn in the books; the Glovers' wavering loyalty shapes Jon's Season 6 campaign.

properties.name: Torrhen's Square
properties.description: Square keep of House Tallhart southwest of Winterfell. Theon's feint against it drew Winterfell's garrison away in Season 2.

properties.name: Barrowton
properties.description: Town built around the great barrow of the First Kings, seat of House Dustin. Book background in the show.

properties.name: Greywater Watch
properties.description: Floating castle of the crannogmen, moving forever through the swamps of the Neck. Home of Howland Reed — the only living witness to the Tower of Joy — and his children Meera and Jojen.

properties.name: Hornwood
properties.description: Seat of House Hornwood between the Dreadfort and Winterfell, swallowed into Bolton hands in the wars. Book background only.

properties.name: Cerwyn
properties.description: Castle of House Cerwyn a half-day's ride from Winterfell. Ramsay flayed Lord Cerwyn for refusing his taxes — as Sansa is grimly told.

properties.name: Oldcastle
properties.description: Seat of House Locke on the White Knife's mouth. Book background only.

properties.name: Ramsgate
properties.description: Holdfast east of White Harbor. Book background only.

properties.name: Widow's Watch
properties.description: Seat of House Flint of Widow's Watch on the stormy eastern cape. Book background only.

properties.name: Flint's Finger
properties.description: Castle of House Flint on the swampy western cape above Cape Kraken. Book background only.

properties.name: Queenscrown
properties.description: Abandoned tower in a lake in the Gift, crowned in gold for a visiting queen. Bran hid here as Jon, held by the wildlings below, refused to kill an innocent — and wargs saved them both.

properties.name: Mole's Town
properties.description: Village half-buried under the Gift, serving the Wall's less official needs. Ygritte's raiders sacked it in Season 4; Sansa met Littlefinger in its tunnels in Season 6.

properties.name: The Nightfort
properties.description: Oldest and most haunted of the Wall's castles, long abandoned. Bran's party crossed beneath the Wall through its hidden Black Gate; Sam and Gilly sheltered in its kitchens.

properties.name: The Shadow Tower
properties.description: Westernmost manned castle of the Night's Watch, guarding the Gorge. Mentioned as one of the three castles still garrisoned.

properties.name: Westwatch-by-the-Bridge
properties.description: Abandoned Night's Watch castle at the Wall's western end. Book background only.

properties.name: Sentinel Stand
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall's western reaches. Book background only.

properties.name: Greyguard
properties.description: Crumbling Wall castle — the posting Ser Alliser used to exile Janos Slynt, before Slynt's refusal cost him his head.

properties.name: Stonedoor
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

properties.name: Hoarfrost Hill
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

properties.name: Icemark
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

properties.name: Deep Lake
properties.description: Wall castle built to replace the sinister Nightfort. Book background only.

properties.name: Queensgate
properties.description: Abandoned Wall castle named for the queen whose crown gilded Queenscrown. Book background only.

properties.name: Oakenshield
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall east of Castle Black. Book background only.

properties.name: Woodswatch-by-the-Pool
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

properties.name: Sable Hall
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

properties.name: Rimegate
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

properties.name: Long Barrow
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall, built over an old barrow. Book background only.

properties.name: The Torches
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall. Book background only.

properties.name: Greenguard
properties.description: Abandoned castle of the Wall near its eastern end. Book background only.

properties.name: Northern Watchtower
properties.description: Lonely watchtower of the northern hills. Book background only.

properties.name: Northern Holdfast
properties.description: Small holdfast of the northern countryside. Book background only.

properties.name: Crofters' Village
properties.description: Village by a lake in the wolfswood — in the books, the frozen camp of Stannis's final campaign.

properties.name: Tumbledown Tower
properties.description: Ruined tower of the wolfswood. Book background only.

properties.name: Stony Shore Village
properties.description: Fishing village of the Stony Shore — the coast Theon raided to prove himself ironborn in Season 2.

properties.name: Highgarden
properties.description: Rose-crowned seat of House Tyrell above the Mander, richest of the great castles. Jaime took it without a siege in Season 7 — and Olenna Tyrell drank his poison and told him it was she who killed Joffrey.

properties.name: Oldtown
properties.description: Oldest and second-greatest city of Westeros, lit by the Hightower's beacon. Sam studied — and stole from — the Citadel's great library here, curing Jorah's grayscale and finding the truth of Jon's birth.

properties.name: Horn Hill
properties.description: Seat of House Tarly in the foothills of the Red Mountains. Sam brought Gilly home to his father's contempt in Season 6 — and left with the family's Valyrian greatsword, Heartsbane.

properties.name: Tumbleton
properties.description: Market town on the Mander, on the road between the Reach and King's Landing. Book background in the show's era.

properties.name: Bitterbridge
properties.description: Castle at the old stone bridge over the Mander where, in the books, Renly's great host camped. The show's Renly camps nearer the coast.

properties.name: Ashford
properties.description: Castle and town on the Cockleswhent, site of a famous tourney of Dunk and Egg legend. Book background only.

properties.name: Cider Hall
properties.description: Apple-sigiled seat of House Fossoway at the meeting of the Mander and the Cockleswhent. Book background only.

properties.name: Brightwater Keep
properties.description: Seat of House Florent, kin by marriage to Stannis Baratheon — Queen Selyse's family castle. Named in the books; background in the show.

properties.name: Fawnton
properties.description: Town of House Cafferen in the eastern Reach. Book background only.

properties.name: Grassy Vale
properties.description: Castle of House Meadows on the upper Mander. Book background only.

properties.name: Bandallon
properties.description: Seat of House Blackbar on the western shore of the Reach. Book background only.

properties.name: Honeyholt
properties.description: Bee-and-honey seat of House Beesbury near Oldtown. Book background only.

properties.name: Blackcrown
properties.description: Castle of House Bulwer southwest of Oldtown. Book background only.

properties.name: Three Towers
properties.description: Seat of House Costayne on the Whispering Sound south of Oldtown. Book background only.

properties.name: Sunflower Hall
properties.description: Seat of House Cuy on the coast east of Oldtown. Book background only.

properties.name: Longtable
properties.description: Castle of House Merryweather on the Mander. Book background only.

properties.name: Goldengrove
properties.description: Seat of House Rowan in the northern Reach. Book background only.

properties.name: Red Lake
properties.description: Castle of House Crane on the shores of Red Lake in the northwestern Reach. Book background only.

properties.name: Old Oak
properties.description: Seat of House Oakheart on the ocean road between the Reach and the Westerlands. Book background only.

properties.name: Tarbeck Hall
properties.description: Ruin of House Tarbeck, destroyed alongside the Reynes of Castamere when Tywin Lannister ended both rebel houses. Its fall echoes in the same grim song.

properties.name: Lord Hewett's Town
properties.description: Harbor town of the Shield Islands guarding the mouth of the Mander. Book background only.

properties.name: Harrenhal
properties.description: Greatest and unluckiest castle in Westeros, its towers melted by dragonfire three centuries ago. Arya served Tywin here as cupbearer; Jaime lost a hand nearby, confessed in its baths and leapt into its bear pit for Brienne.

properties.name: Riverrun
properties.description: Moated seat of House Tully at the joining of two rivers. Robb was proclaimed King in the North here; years later Jaime ended the Blackfish's last stand by turning Edmure against his own walls.

properties.name: The Twins
properties.description: Twin castles bridging the Green Fork, toll-gate of the north and seat of Walder Frey. The Red Wedding drowned its hall in Stark blood — and Arya Stark returned twice to collect the debt.

properties.name: Crossroads Inn
properties.description: The famous inn where the kingsroad meets the river road. Catelyn seized Tyrion here; Arya reclaimed Needle from Polliver here; and Hot Pie bakes here still, twice pointing Brienne and Arya on their way.

properties.name: Stoney Sept
properties.description: Largest town of the riverlands, remembered for the Battle of the Bells in Robert's Rebellion. Book background in the show's era.

properties.name: High Heart
properties.description: Sacred hill ringed by weirwood stumps, haunted by old gods' dreams. The Brotherhood's ghost-seeress dwells here in the books; the show keeps only its wild riverland setting.

properties.name: Hollow Hill
properties.description: Hidden cave-hall of the Brotherhood Without Banners, where the Hound was tried by fire against Beric Dondarrion and Arya watched a dead man rise again.

properties.name: Stone Mill
properties.description: Mill on the Red Fork where Edmure Tully threw back the Mountain's raiders — a 'victory' that wrecked Robb's trap and cost the Stark cause dearly.

properties.name: Darry
properties.description: Castle of House Darry near the kingsroad. The confrontation over Arya's direwolf happened in its lands in Season 1. Otherwise book background.

properties.name: Maidenpool
properties.description: Port town on the Bay of Crabs where Florian first saw Jonquil bathing, or so the songs say. Book background in the show.

properties.name: Seagard
properties.description: Fortified port of House Mallister, raised to guard against ironborn raids. Book background only.

properties.name: Stone Hedge
properties.description: Seat of House Bracken on the Red Fork, ancient rivals of the Blackwoods across the river. Book background only.

properties.name: Raventree Hall
properties.description: Seat of House Blackwood beneath a dead weirwood full of ravens. Book background only.

properties.name: Acorn Hall
properties.description: Keep of House Smallwood in the riverland woods, a stop on Arya's book travels with the Brotherhood. Background in the show.

properties.name: Pinkmaiden
properties.description: Castle of House Piper on the Red Fork. Book background only.

properties.name: Antlers
properties.description: Castle of House Buckwell northeast of King's Landing. Book background only.

properties.name: Sow's Horn
properties.description: Holdfast of House Hogg near the crownland border. Book background only.

properties.name: Brindlewood
properties.description: Village on the kingsroad approach to King's Landing. Book background only.

properties.name: Ivy Inn
properties.description: Roadside inn on the kingsroad south of the Trident. Book background only.

properties.name: Trident Village
properties.description: One of the countless riverland villages burned and re-burned as armies crossed the Trident — the war's quiet casualties.

properties.name: Riverlands Holdfast
properties.description: Fortified refuge typical of the riverland smallfolk, offering thin protection from the War of the Five Kings.

properties.name: Rushing Falls
properties.description: Falls of the upper Blackwater Rush. Book background geography.

properties.name: Tumbler's Falls
properties.description: River town at the falls of the Blackwater Rush. Book background only.

properties.name: Riverland Sept
properties.description: Country sept of the riverlands — kin to the quiet septry where the Hound found brief peace with Brother Ray's flock before the Brotherhood's renegades came.

properties.name: Mummer's Ford
properties.description: Ford on the Red Fork where, in the books, Beric Dondarrion's party was ambushed by the Mountain — the errand Ned sent him on in Season 1.

properties.name: Sherrer
properties.description: Village put to the sword in the Mountain's raids — its survivors petitioned Ned Stark on the Iron Throne in Season 1.

properties.name: Wendish Town
properties.description: Riverland town burned in Gregor Clegane's raids, named among the ruins reported to the Iron Throne.

properties.name: Lord Goodbrook's Village
properties.description: Village of a minor riverland house. Book background only.

properties.name: Sallydance
properties.description: Riverland village of the books, plundered in the war. Book background only.

properties.name: Lady of the Leaves' Village
properties.description: Hidden treetop village of war refugees from the books. Book background only.

properties.name: Lord Lychester's Keep
properties.description: Small keep of a broken riverland house. Book background only.

properties.name: Trident Hamlet
properties.description: Nameless hamlet of the war-torn Trident country. Book background only.

properties.name: Inn of the Lion Banner
properties.description: Roadside inn that hosted Lannister soldiery in the war years — the kind of place Arya and the Hound learned to eat at quietly.

properties.name: Inn of the Kneeling Man
properties.description: Trident inn named for the king who knelt to Aegon the Conqueror. In the books, Arya's party is taken by the Brotherhood here.

properties.name: Brotherhood Hideout
properties.description: One of the Brotherhood Without Banners' scattered boltholes in the riverland hills — the outlaws who fight for the smallfolk of no king.

properties.name: Lord Harroway's Town
properties.description: Trident crossing town of the books, half-drowned by the wars' seasons. Book background only.

properties.name: Quiet Isle
properties.description: Monastic island at the mouth of the Trident where broken men heal in silence. The show's Brother Ray sept storyline borrows its spirit.

properties.name: Fairmarket
properties.description: Market town on the Blue Fork. Book background only.

properties.name: Oldstones
properties.description: Ruined hilltop castle of the ancient river kings, where in the books Robb holds council. Background in the show.

properties.name: Palisade Village
properties.description: Stockaded village of the northern riverlands. Book background only.

properties.name: Pennytree
properties.description: Village around an ancient oak studded with pennies for luck. Book background only.

properties.name: Storm's End
properties.description: Ancient storm-proof seat of House Baratheon, raised by legend against the wrath of the gods. Renly and Stannis parleyed beneath its walls, Melisandre birthed the shadow in the caves below, and Gendry was legitimized its lord by King Bran's council era.

properties.name: Evenfall Hall
properties.description: Seat of House Tarth on the Sapphire Isle — Brienne's home, which she left behind for Renly's colors and never truly returned to.

properties.name: Summerhall
properties.description: Burned summer palace of the Targaryens, where a king died trying to wake dragons from eggs. A ghost story by the show's era, known from Targaryen history.

properties.name: Blackhaven
properties.description: Seat of House Dondarrion in the Dornish Marches — Beric's home, which he left on Ned Stark's errand and never saw again.

properties.name: Nightsong
properties.description: March castle of House Caron guarding the passes into Dorne. Book background only.

properties.name: Haystack Hall
properties.description: Seat of House Errol in the stormland interior. Book background; never seen in the show.

properties.name: Bronzegate
properties.description: Castle of House Buckler on the road between King's Landing and Storm's End. Book background only.

properties.name: Felwood
properties.description: Keep of House Fell in the rainwood's northern reaches. Book background only.

properties.name: Griffin's Roost
properties.description: Cliff-perched seat of the exiled House Connington on Cape Wrath. Central to a book plotline the show cut entirely.

properties.name: Rain House
properties.description: Storm-lashed castle of House Wylde on the rainwood coast. Book background only.

properties.name: Greenstone
properties.description: Seat of House Estermont on its island off the stormland coast — kin to Robert Baratheon's mother. Book background only.

properties.name: Weeping Tower
properties.description: Lonely watchtower of the stormland coast. Book background only.

properties.name: Mistwood
properties.description: Castle of House Mertyns deep in the rainwood. Book background only.

properties.name: Stonehelm
properties.description: Seat of House Swann above the Slayne in the marches. Balon Swann serves in the books' Kingsguard; the show leaves the family behind.

properties.name: Crow's Nest
properties.description: Keep of House Morrigen in the stormland hills. Book background only.

properties.name: Grandview
properties.description: Holdfast town of House Grandison. Book background only.

properties.name: Parchments
properties.description: Seat of House Penrose on the stormland coast. Book background only.

properties.name: The Eyrie
properties.description: Seat of House Arryn, perched high atop the Giant's Lance and long thought impregnable. Tyrion was locked in its sky cells and won his freedom when Bronn fought for him, and Littlefinger later shoved Lysa Arryn to her death through the Moon Door.

properties.name: The Bloody Gate
properties.description: Fortified pass guarding the only road into the Vale, where countless armies have broken themselves against the mountains. Arya and the Hound were turned away here after learning of Lysa Arryn's death — prompting Arya's infamous laughing fit.

properties.name: Runestone
properties.description: Ancient seat of House Royce, one of the oldest lines in the Vale. Littlefinger left Robin Arryn here to be fostered by Lord Yohn Royce, and later returned to pry the boy — and the knights of the Vale — loose to march north for Sansa.

properties.name: Gulltown
properties.description: The Vale's chief port and only true city, held by House Grafton for the Arryns. Its harbor links the mountain kingdom to the trade of the Narrow Sea.

properties.name: Strongsong
properties.description: Mountain seat of House Belmore, bannermen of House Arryn in the high valleys of the Vale.

properties.name: Heart's Home
properties.description: Seat of House Corbray, an old knightly line of the Vale sworn to the Arryns and famed for the Valyrian steel sword Lady Forlorn.

properties.name: Redfort
properties.description: Red-stone castle of House Redfort, one of the most respected of the Vale houses sworn to the Eyrie.

properties.name: Ironoaks
properties.description: Seat of House Waynwood, proud Arryn bannermen. Lady Anya Waynwood was among the Vale lords who questioned Littlefinger over Lysa Arryn's death at the Eyrie.

properties.name: Old Anchor
properties.description: Coastal keep of House Melcolm on the eastern shore of the Vale, sworn to House Arryn.

properties.name: Longbow Hall
properties.description: Seat of House Hunter, Vale bannermen of House Arryn whose sigil of five arrows honors the family's famed archers.

properties.name: Snakewood
properties.description: Forest seat of House Lynderly in the northern Vale, a minor house sworn to the Eyrie.

properties.name: Coldwater
properties.description: Seat of House Coldwater, a lesser house of the northern Vale sworn to House Royce of Runestone.

properties.name: Baelish Keep
properties.description: A small flint tower on the smallest of the Fingers, the humble ancestral holding where Petyr Baelish was born. Its meagerness fueled Littlefinger's lifelong hunger to climb far above his station.

properties.name: Sisterton
properties.description: Port town on Sweetsister, largest of the Three Sisters in the Bite. A notorious haunt of smugglers, ruled by House Borrell under Arryn overlordship.

properties.name: Saltpans
properties.description: Small port town on the Bay of Crabs at the mouth of the Trident, known for its salt works and modest harbor.

properties.name: Wickenden
properties.description: Castle of House Waxley on the southern shore of the Bay of Crabs, famed for its scented beeswax candles.

properties.name: Dyre Den
properties.description: A brooding castle of three crooked towers on the cliffs of Crackclaw Point, held by House Brune.

properties.name: Crakehall
properties.description: Seat of House Crakehall, longtime Lannister bannermen, in the forested south of the westerlands along the ocean road.

properties.name: Cornfield
properties.description: Castle of House Swyft, bannermen sworn to Casterly Rock, in the southern westerlands.

properties.name: Silverhill
properties.description: Seat of House Serrett, Lannister bannermen, in the hills of the southeastern westerlands.

properties.name: Clegane Hall
properties.description: Modest keep of House Clegane, the Lannister retainers who produced Gregor 'the Mountain' and Sandor 'the Hound.' It was here, as Littlefinger tells Sansa, that young Gregor held his brother's face in the fire for playing with his toy, leaving the Hound scarred for life.

properties.name: Lannisport
properties.description: Great port city on the Sunset Sea in the shadow of Casterly Rock, home to the Lannister fleet and the merchant wealth of the west. Often referenced in the show but never depicted on screen.

properties.name: Feastfires
properties.description: Castle of House Prester on a headland of the western coast, overlooking the Sunset Sea.

properties.name: Kayce
properties.description: Small port town on the westerlands coast near Feastfires, north of Lannisport.

properties.name: Oxcross
properties.description: Site of Robb Stark's surprise night attack on a Lannister host camped deep inside the westerlands. The battle's grisly aftermath opens 'Garden of Bones' (S2E4), where Robb first meets Talisa tending the wounded.

properties.name: Sarsfield
properties.description: Castle of House Sarsfield, Lannister bannermen, on the river road north of Lannisport.

properties.name: Deep Den
properties.description: Castle of House Lydden astride the goldroad, in the mountains between the westerlands and the crownlands.

properties.name: Hornvale
properties.description: Seat of House Brax in the mountainous east of the westerlands, near the riverlands border.

properties.name: Golden Tooth
properties.description: Castle of House Lefford guarding the mountain pass between the westerlands and the riverlands — the gateway through which Lannister armies march east to war.

properties.name: Wayfarer's Rest
properties.description: Castle of House Vance near the Golden Tooth, on the contested border between the westerlands and the riverlands.

properties.name: Castamere
properties.description: Ruined seat of House Reyne, exterminated root and branch by a young Tywin Lannister when they rose against his father. The massacre is immortalized in 'The Rains of Castamere,' the Lannister anthem played moments before the Red Wedding.

properties.name: Pendric Hills
properties.description: Range of hills in the northern westerlands, part of the gold-rich uplands that fed the Lannister mines.

properties.name: The Crag
properties.description: Half-ruined castle of House Westerling on the northern coast of the westerlands. In the books Robb Stark is wounded and wed here, a storyline the show replaced with Talisa of Volantis.

properties.name: Banefort
properties.description: Northernmost castle of the westerlands, seat of House Banefort, facing the ironborn across Ironman's Bay.

properties.name: Ashemark
properties.description: Seat of House Marbrand, prominent Lannister bannermen, in the hills of the northern westerlands.

properties.name: Nunn's Deep
properties.description: One of the gold mines that built the Lannister fortune. As Tywin confesses in season 4, the westerlands mines ran dry three years before the War of the Five Kings.

properties.name: Faircastle
properties.description: Castle of House Farman on Fair Isle, off the western coast of the westerlands in the Sunset Sea.

properties.name: Casterly Rock
properties.description: Ancestral stronghold of House Lannister, carved into a colossal rock above the Sunset Sea atop the gold mines that made the family the richest in Westeros. Grey Worm and the Unsullied stormed it in 'The Queen's Justice' (S7E3) through the sewer passage Tyrion once built, only to find Jaime had left a token garrison and marched the real Lannister army on Highgarden.
